behavior_constraints: Config is loaded from /app/config/services.toml in TOML format with global settings and per-service endpoints
TCP health check succeeds if connection establishes within 1 second
HTTP health check sends GET to http://<address><health_path>, succeeds only if status 200 and body contains 'ok' case-insensitively, 2s timeout
Exec health check runs health_cmd via shell, succeeds if exit code 0, 3s timeout
Endpoints start as 'unknown'; healthy_threshold consecutive successes transition to 'healthy'
unhealthy_threshold consecutive failures transition a 'healthy' endpoint to 'unhealthy'; counters reset on transitions
Circuit breaker opens immediately when health transitions healthy->unhealthy
Circuit transitions open->half_open after circuit_breaker_timeout_ms elapsed while open
half_open allows at most one probe connection; success closes circuit, failure reopens with restarted timeout
Health recovery to 'healthy' while circuit is 'open' does NOT close the circuit

instruction_head:
# Service Mesh Health Router

Build a service mesh health monitoring and traffic routing system in Go. The system consists of three integrated components that must work together end-to-end: a **health monitor daemon**, a **traffic router/proxy**, and a **CLI control tool**. All three share state through a local Unix domain socket protocol.

behavior_constraints: Token bucket uses lazy continuous refill: tokens = min(burst, tokens + rps * elapsed_seconds) with no background refill goroutine
rate_limit_burst is independently configurable from rate_limit_rps (e.g., rps=2, burst=8)
Rate limiting is applied before endpoint selection
A rate-limited rejection must NOT count as a failure toward any endpoint's circuit breaker
rate_limited counter increments on immediate no-token rejections and queue-full rejections
queue_timeouts counter increments when a queued connection exceeds rate_limit_queue_timeout_ms
When rate_limit_queue_depth > 0 and queue not full, connection waits up to rate_limit_queue_timeout_ms for a token
When rate limit parameters change via set_rate_limit or reload, current token count is preserved but capped to the new burst
Retry selects a different endpoint, never the same one consecutively
Retry delay = retry_delay_ms * retry_backoff_multiplier^(attempt-1), capped at retry_max_delay_ms, and is a real wait

instruction_head:
# Per-Service Rate Limiting and Connection Retry

Add per-service rate limiting using a token bucket algorithm and automatic connection retry with exponential backoff to the mesh router.

## Rate Limiting

Each service gets a configurable token bucket rate limiter applied before endpoint selection. New config fields on each `[[service]]`:

- `rate_limit_rps` (int) — tokens per second; 0 means unlimited (default)
- `rate_limit_burst` (int) — max bucket size; defaults to `rate_limit_rps` if omitte
